newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Jackson's in-law dodges media in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Jackson's in-law dodges media in Cyprus.

text.p: Retired American pilot Gordon Rowe is dodging the unwanted attention brought by the marriage of his 37-year-old daughter Debbie to pop superstar Michael Jackson last week.

After two decades of obscure retirement in Cyprus -- even fellow villagers barely know him -- the stooped 67-year-old father-in-law of the eccentric entertainer made no secret on Tuesday he would prefer to return to anonymity.
Rowe, bespectacled with a shock of white hair and a goatee beard, appeared at the open balcony window of his modest two-storey house on a narrow street in Ayios Tychonas village after several calls.
"I am sitting down for lunch now," Rowe, leaning on a walking stick, called down to two reporters. The balcony was cluttered with gardening equipment, a washing line and a couple of deck chairs.

He inclined his head sharply sideways towards the Toyota Corolla in the driveway, implying they should move along. A suggestion of an interview later with the father of the nurse who married the pop star was curtly brushed aside.
"No thank you," Rowe shouted firmly but politely over the excited barking of an Alsatian dog belonging to a Greek Cypriot neighbour.
Rowe hobbled back into the dimly-lit traditional house without another word, leaving reporters outside in an overgrown garden with a broken television set and the sound of the barking dog.
The former pilot for a Lebanese freight airline, who is divorced from Debby's mother, has lived on the east Mediterranean island for the past 20 years.

In the mid-80s he moved to the hillside village of Ayios Tychonas, 70 kilometres (45 miles) southwest of the capital Nicosia, one of many Cypriot villages that have been turned into retirement boltholes for foreigners.
The lady at the local post office knew him as "Mr Gordon" and appeared to be the only villager who knew where he lived. Few others knew him by name.
"He keeps himself to himself," said one villager. "I didn't even know he was an American."
Andreas Antoniou, owner of a coffee shop round the corner from Rowe's home, said: "We have so many foreigners living in the village.
"But Michael Jackson's father in law? I thought he was married to that (Lisa-Marie) Presley woman," he said, looking puzzled.
